content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Lawton

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: The PMP credential requires a secondary degree plus documented project-management experience, or a high school diploma with additional years of experience. PMI sets specific thresholds for both education and hours managed. Verify your qualifications against PMI's current requirements before enrolling in Granite PM Academy's training.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Granite PM Academy delivers the mandatory 35 contact hours via live-virtual, instructor-led instruction. You'll attend interactive sessions online, ask questions in real time, and receive certification of completion. This formal education covers the PMBOK® Guide framework and prepares you directly for the exam.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your 35 hours, submit your formal application to PMI, including proof of education and project experience. Pay the associated exam fee through PMI's portal. Allow time for PMI to review and approve your application before scheduling your test.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Granite PM Academy provides exam-preparation resources, practice questions, and coaching to reinforce key concepts. You'll sit for the computer-based PMP exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. The exam tests your knowledge of project-management principles, tools, and real-world application.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: PMP certification is valid for three years. During each renewal cycle, you must earn professional development units (PDUs) through training, volunteer work, or certifications. Granite PM Academy and PMI offer multiple pathways to earn PDUs and keep your credential active and current.
